updates.note: On anchorage waits: 'A queue is what success looks like at a port with one channel'; says buyers now budget for the wait.
Said the military outload goes on the same schedule as commercial cargo and crude customers should not expect disruption.
Said the brigade's port movement is planned for late summer and the unit will 'be ready when the port is ready.'
Explained that exporters and refiners share one channel: 'People talk about the export story and forget there is a refining town at the end of that channel.'
Told Gulfwater why standby relief contracts are signed in August: 'The boxes are the easy part. The lane is the hard part'; hopes the contracts go unused.
Said the port plans for relief cargo every year and that 'the limiting factor after a storm is usually the channel, not the dock.'
Described the daily vessel lineup as 'a puzzle we solve every day'; said planning for the Fort Hood brigade's outload is on track.
On hurricane-season risk at a port near capacity: 'The outlook doesn't change today's cargo. It changes how much you want riding on one outlet in September.'
On the monthly export high: 'It was a strong month, and it was a safe month.'
Told Gulfwater the port's share, about half of U.S. crude exports, means 'when Corpus Christi is busy, the whole export system is busy.'
With Rafael a hurricane: 'The market is watching one thing, which is whether the Coast Guard sets a port condition at Corpus Christi.'
Said Gulf Relief Logistics booked relief cargo on MV Gulf Provider: 'If it comes here, the ship will be waiting for the channel like everybody else.'
Said nothing had changed in port status and customers should watch for the Captain of the Port's notices.
Said the port is open and loading and that any change will come from the Coast Guard Captain of the Port.
On the cone covering Corpus Christi: 'Now it is a planning problem. The crude that loads this week is safe. The crude that was going to load next week is a question.'
Announced Port Condition Yankee: port closed to inbound traffic; ocean-going vessels departing.
As exports halted: 'About half of U.S. crude exports just stopped moving. The only number that matters now is how many days.'
On the eve of landfall: 'Zulu is the end of the part you can plan. The rest is what the storm leaves.'
Confirmed Condition Zulu and that two laden tankers were approved to remain moored at an Inner Harbor terminal.
Gave the Unified Command estimate: 'about 9,000 barrels and it is an estimate'; would not speculate on cause.
Said boom goes in the water as soon as wind allows; crews staging equipment.
Said Rendal Terminals is cooperating fully and will not comment on the cause.
Said Rendal Terminals is cooperating fully with the Unified Command; declined to discuss cause.
On the spill's market meaning: 'Yesterday this was a hurricane closure with a known shape. Today it is a spill response, and those don't come with a schedule.'
Said the channel reopens only after it is surveyed and the spill is contained; no date.
Said the port is supporting the Unified Command and 'will be ready to work' when the Coast Guard reopens the channel.
On ships returning to the anchorage: 'The ships are back. The port isn't'; says the market has stopped asking 'which day' and started asking 'which week.'
Said the channel stays closed while it is surveyed and the spill is contained; no date.
Listed four restart conditions: surveyed channel, contained spill, utilities, people; 'Any one of those can hold up the other three.'
Company statement day: 'Our remote-maintenance credentials were misused. We have revoked all remote access to customer vessels'; does not know by whom.
Said the vendor disclosure adds a vetting question for charterers: 'Who can touch the cargo system, and from where?'
Eleven days into the halt: 'The system is bending. It is not rerouting. There is no second Corpus Christi to send it to.'
On post-storm channel depths: 'I would not assume the bottom is where the chart says until someone has measured it.'
Said reopening comes in stages and 'the survey sets the pace.'
Said damaged plant pumps need replacement parts and temporary pumps limit capacity; apologized and asked residents to keep conserving and boiling water.
Noted that water is on the restart checklist for industry along the channel: 'It is not a crude number, but it is on the list.'
Confirmed the owners' claims center is open for cleanup and property damage claims; urged people to document losses.
On liability: 'The law says who pays first. The investigation decides who pays last.'
On the Districts 3 and 4 notice: low pressure means contamination cannot be ruled out; 'This is a precaution, and it is a necessary one.'
Confirmed only that the FBI is investigating reports of unauthorized drone activity in the Corpus Christi area and asked for tips.
Confirmed the FBI is investigating reports of unauthorized drone activity in the Corpus Christi area; no further comment.
On refiners during the closure: 'An exporter is a tap. A refinery is a machine. You can shut a tap. A machine wants to keep running.'
On the power setback: 'Two weeks ago I had the grid in the solved column. I have moved it back.'
General advice after the governor's directive: inventory remote access, remove what is not needed, report anomalies; would not discuss either investigation.
On containment: 'This is the first item to come off the list since the storm. It is not the last item.'
Said containment is a milestone, shoreline work continues and the fishing closure stays until testing supports lifting it.
Frustrated by the wait: 'I have forty boxes of relief supplies looking at the beach'; MV Gulf Provider still at the offshore anchorage.
Said the port and pilots have a restart sequence drafted and relief cargo 'is on the list near the top.'
Fifth week of the halt: 'Every one of these has a version of the same answer. In progress, no date.'
On the cyber emergency amendment: 'I cover crude. This month I am reading utility notices, because the port does not restart on crude alone.'
Two days into the partial reopening: 'Ships are moving. Not as many as we want, and not as fast.'
On the partial reopening: 'Open is not the same as normal. The market got the first word this week. It is still waiting for the second.'
On the day his containers landed, Oct. 17: 'Those boxes were booked five days before landfall. They touched the dock today'; says the lesson is about depending on one channel.
Said working the relief ship was a priority within the limits of a partial reopening; the backlog 'is real and it is shrinking.'
On the port's counter-drone initiative: 'We would rather know what is flying over the docks than guess'; would not discuss sensor locations.
On the pump parts arriving: 'The parts are here. Now we install them and test, and the notice stays until the tests pass.'
Ten days into the partial reopening: 'The city is nearly back. The port is half back. The half that is missing is the inner channel.'
Said pilots reported GPS interference within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi and that flights continue using backup navigation.
Declined to discuss the interference reports; said mariners are always expected to fix position by all available means.
On lifting the last notice: 'You can drink the water. Thank you for boiling it for as long as you did.'
Described the blast to Gulfwater: off the port bow, around 1 a.m.; 'First thing you do is count heads'; two of his crew hurt; would not guess at a cause.
Said the channel is closed by Captain of the Port order, the cause is unknown and there is no reopening time.
Said investigators traced the GPS interference to a transmitter in a parked vehicle in an industrial area near a fuel terminal off the Inner Harbor; investigation ongoing; would not discuss evidence.
Confirmed the interference reports have stopped.
Told Sabal the spoofed identity appeared near the entrance channel two weeks before the blast: 'I can tell you where the signal was. I cannot tell you what it means.'
On the security question: 'After the storm the question was when. Now there is a second question, which is whether.'
Off the water while Corrin Bay is out of service; visits Fontenot most days; on the Navy finding: 'Somebody put that there. I have been turning that over for a week.'
Spoke by phone Tuesday, Nov. 2: remembers the noise and being on the deck; broken arm and concussion; grateful to Dupree; 'I want to go back. Not this week.'
On the market facing a crisis abroad and a closed channel: 'Either one alone is a story. Together they are a week nobody wants to trade.'
Announced Navy teams found a second explosive device near the entrance channel and rendered it safe; search continues; would not describe the device.
After the second device: 'One device, you can tell yourself it was the only one. Two, and the question becomes how many.'
Explained the closure order: it binds every vessel, commercial or recreational; ends by written notice; 'We ask operators to wait for the notice.'
Said Navy teams will keep searching until the search is complete and would not describe methods or what was found.
On the end of a security closure: 'The reopening notice is one document. The decision to send a ship is another, and somebody's underwriter is in that conversation.'
Says the search is the right response and public data cannot shorten it: 'There is nothing in a tracking feed that tells you a channel is clean.'
On day 13 of the closure: 'Berths are clear and terminals are staffed. The plan for the first days is written. We need the entrance.'
On storage during the second halt: 'In September the tanks started with room. This time they started half recovered.'
Customers' cargo held again by the channel closure: 'I told my customers in October it would not happen twice. I have stopped saying that.'
Announced the Captain of the Port lifted the closure order; first transits sequenced with pilots.
Said the Navy's sweep of the channel is complete and the channel is clear; would not describe what was found beyond earlier statements.
On reopening: 'Berths are clear and terminals are staffed. Today we work the plan.'
First full day after reopening: 'Tankers out, tankers in, and the Army's cargo loading. That is a good day.'
On the restart: 'This restart is cleaner than October's. One constraint, and it is gone.'
On the 60-day assessment: 'The emergency is over. The monitoring is not, and neither is the claims process.'
Urged fishers and shoreline businesses to file lost-income claims and keep records; closures themselves are set by state health and wildlife agencies.
Said Rendal Terminals continues to cooperate fully and referred claims questions to the claims center.
Back on the water since mid-November on another Laguna Towing boat; 'The work is the same. I look at the water differently'; Fontenot still in a cast.
Arm still in a cast; Dupree says he is 'mending and bored, which is the right order.'
Says all customer remote access remains revoked two months on; technicians attend vessels in person; 'Slower and more expensive is acceptable'; still does not know who misused the credentials.
General advice on vendor access: know who connects, when and why; be able to cut it quickly.
Rewriting his hurricane playbook around a plan B that does not depend on one channel: split cargo, an inland staging point, a second port named in the contract.
Said the port understands customers planning alternatives and wants to earn the cargo back by being reliable.
Disputed the Navy suspension: 'All product Quellmar delivered met specifications. We expect the review to confirm that.'
Confirmed the station suspended its emergency fuel supplier pending a fuel quality review; 'no impact to operations.'
On the tanker investigation's timeline: 'It will take the time it takes'; findings released when complete, not in installments.
Said Quellmar will cooperate with the inspector general's review and stands by its product.
On whether the AIS anomaly is linked to the blast: 'The timing is a fact. A link is a claim. I have the first and not the second.'
Confirmed the Navy ordered a security review at its Texas air stations, citing drone reports and the channel attack; would not discuss scope or timeline.
Said the Navy review does not change port conditions at Corpus Christi.
Year-end view: 'The volume came back. The assumption did not. Every buyer I talk to has a second port written down now.'
Said the port is closing the year with customers shipping and 'will spend next year earning the word reliable back.'
Confirmed FBI agents executed search warrants at Quellmar Fuel Partners and Vantorra Restoration; no comment on what was sought.
Quellmar responded in a written statement only: its product met specifications and it is cooperating.
On the joint advisory: 'We are asking operators to know who holds a key to the cargo system and to be able to take it back.'
On charterers and the advisory: 'An advisory is voluntary. A charterer's questionnaire is not.'
On the Dec. 28 advisory: 'An advisory is only useful if somebody opens the access list and reads it.'
Says operators should keep their own record of AIS anomalies near the entrance: 'If you see a ship in two places, write it down and send it in.'
On hardening the plant's power feeds: 'The pumps were damaged because the power failed first. We are starting where the failure started.'
On the forfeiture filing: 'All product Quellmar delivered met specifications'; the company will respond in court.
Said the agencies reopened only what testing supports; urged claimants to keep records and check closure maps.
Said Rendal Terminals continues to cooperate and would not comment on claims or the investigation.
Four months on: 'The channel is open and the port condition is normal'; would not discuss the security review.
Said the port is taking part in the security review and 'would rather be asked hard questions now than in September.'
Four months on: 'We always knew the share was large. We learned what it feels like when the share is zero.'
